Coverage links the assault to Ukraine's Patriot interceptor shortage, with Zelenskyy calling on allies to replenish stockpiles. A related thread on Russia's strained oil industry has developed further: Ukrainian strikes have knocked out nearly a third of Russia's major refineries, sparking fuel shortages, petrol station fights, and arrests of complaining citizens. On Friday, Israeli settlers and soldiers killed two Palestinians in separate West Bank incidents: 17-year-old Karim Sanad Shalaldeh, shot by settlers, and 58-year-old Fathi Khazem, killed by Israeli forces. Video also emerged of Israeli soldiers themselves throwing belongings out of a besieged Palestinian home in Qusra, alongside settler sieges. Palestinian American homeowner Louai (Loui) Abo Ridi, back from Ohio after 10 days under siege, has directly confronted settlers outside his home despite Israeli military deployment, demanding protection from Israeli forces and the U.S. government. A new Yesh Din report finds settler attacks in Palestinian-administered West Bank areas have almost doubled since 2025 amid a self-proclaimed 'great settlement revolution,' with AJLabs analysis putting the rate at six attacks a day. Separately, settler children attacked a Red Crescent ambulance, the Board of Peace reversed course on a Gaza disarmament deal, Christian families report growing pressure to leave, and Israel opened tenders for over 1,200 homes in the E1 settlement, prompting France, Germany, Britain and Italy to join Europe and Canada in condemning the plan as making Palestinian statehood impossible. An Israeli minister also faces backlash over a gallows site with a 'viewing booth' for hanging Palestinians.

clusters.title: Tropical Storm Moke expected to bring up to 15 inches of rain in Hawaii

items.title: Tropical Storm Moke expected to bring up to 15 inches of rain in Hawaii

ledger.what_new: New storm, Tropical Storm Moke, forecast to bring up to 15 inches of rain to Hawaii.
ledger.unique: Specific rainfall forecast of 15 inches from Moke.

clusters.state_of_play: Indonesia's twin earthquakes (7.7 and 6.4 magnitude) have killed at least 68 people, with thousands still awaiting aid and homeless on Flores Island days after the quake, overshadowing the country's Independence Day. Meanwhile Hurricane Lala weakened to a tropical storm after its eye passed about 30 miles off Hawaii's Big Island without direct landfall, avoiding the first direct hurricane hit on the island in over a century; it still lashed the island with hurricane-force gusts and nearly 3 feet of rain, causing flooding and mudslides, at least one death, more than 100 homes damaged or lost, damage to bridges, and over 180,000 households losing power, per Gov. Josh Green. The storm has since restrengthened into a Category 3 hurricane and moved west, away from Hawaii, where crews are working to restore power and clear roads. Now, just days later, Tropical Storm Moke is poised to hit Hawaii, forecast to bring up to 15 inches of rain and strong winds, with the Big Island again expected to bear the brunt as it passes south late Saturday into Sunday, raising fresh flooding and mudslide concerns in areas already battered by Lala. The storm also struck Maui, stranding tourists, and officials issued a major disaster declaration. Meanwhile the same system fueled the worst Indiana flooding in over 30 years, with the broader Midwest death toll now at least 7, including at least six in Indiana—a 4-year-old boy, two men, and three women—since storms began Aug. 11, per state homeland security spokesperson Liz Woods. Floodwaters peaked along Indianapolis's White River after Mayor Joe Hogsett ordered evacuations and crews conducted water rescues, with rain expected to ease in the capital region on Sunday though the National Weather Service warns flash flooding remains possible across central Indiana. Indiana's governor says the federal government has promised assistance, with more heavy rain expected across Indiana, Illinois and neighboring states this weekend.

clusters.title: Judge denies Karmelo Anthony's appeal for a new trial in killing of Austin Metcalf

items.title: Judge denies Karmelo Anthony's appeal for a new trial in killing of Austin Metcalf

clusters.state_of_play: A Texas judge denied Karmelo Anthony's request for a new trial in the 2025 fatal stabbing of classmate Austin Metcalf at a Frisco track meet; Anthony was convicted by a Collin County jury in June and sentenced to 35 years. A two-day hearing included testimony from Anthony's former lawyers about a disputed unwritten deal with prosecutors that kept him from testifying, and the denial was issued by a newly appointed judge.
